महाभारत के कृष्णा यानी Nitish Bharadwaj ने निर्देशक Nitesh Tiwari की फिल्म Ramayana को लेकर बड़ा बयान दे दिया है! 🔥

NDTV को दिए एक इंटरव्यू में Nitish Bharadwaj का दावा है कि यह एक 'एजेंडा फिल्म' की तरह लगती है। उनका आरोप है कि फिल्म में Ravana को एक उदार और मार्क्सवादी नेता की तरह हीरो बनाकर दिखाया गया है, जबकि Lord Ram के किरदार को बेहद कमजोर और सामान्य इंसान की तरह पेश किया गया है। 😲

Nitish Bharadwaj का यह भी कहना है कि Luxembourg, UAE और Singapore से आए प्रोडक्शन फंड की सरकार को जांच करनी चाहिए, क्योंकि सिनेमा के जरिए भारतीय सभ्यता को कमतर दिखाने की कोशिश हो रही है। बता दें कि इससे पहले उन्होंने फिल्म के trailer की तारीफ की थी। 🎬

सिर्फ Nitish ही नहीं, बल्कि Mukesh Khanna और Sunil Lahri ने भी Sai Pallavi के लड़ाकू सीता वाले किरदार पर आपत्ति जताई है। दूसरी तरफ, इन विवादों के बीच भी Ramayana ने domestic box office पर ₹860 करोड़ और worldwide ₹1,500 करोड़ की रिकॉर्ड कमाई कर ली है। 📈

क्या आप Nitish Bharadwaj के इन बयानों से सहमत हैं? अपनी राय कमेंट्स में जरूर शेयर करें! 👇

ctx.title: Mahabharat's Lord Krishna, Nitish Bharadwaj, calls Ramayana an ‘agenda film’, slams Ravana's portrayal as a hero
ctx.summary: The Mahabharat actor says the film diminishes Lord Rama and presents Ravana as a hero, calling its portrayal agenda-driven.
ctx.text:
Mahabharat actor Nitish Bharadwaj has strongly criticised Nitesh Tiwari 's Ramayana. While the film received largely positive reviews from critics, Nitish called out the makers for portraying Ravana as an exceptionally liberal, socially just and fair ruler, arguing that this undermines the very purpose of Lord Vishnu's avatar. He further said that the film "seems like an agenda film".
Nitish, best known for playing Lord Krishna in BR Chopra's Mahabharat, had earlier praised the trailer of Ramayana and predicted international success for the film. However, the final product has disappointed him. In an interview with NDTV, Nitish objected to Lord Rama's portrayal and said, "Lord Ram has been brought down to a minuscule, normal human being who has a deadpan face. That's not Ram. Lord Ram is about maryada."
He added that the portrayal of Ram leaving Ayodhya in tears fails to reflect the Ikshvaku clan's code of honour.
Nitish further criticised the film for showing Ravana as a hero and said, "Ravana's negatives were not shown at all. His character comes across like a Marxist communist leader. This weakling that you showed as Lord Ram is going to kill Ravan. You are making a hero out of a villain and a villain out of a hero."
He further argued that the younger generation, which "does not read", could spend the next two years admiring Ravana as a "cool dude". He questioned how the makers would then portray Ram defeating Ravana in Part 2. Nitish also claimed that money had come into the production company from Luxembourg, the UAE and Singapore. He compared what he described as "agenda people" to "the new British", alleging that cinema was being used to diminish Indian civilisation. He urged the government to "do the money trail" into the film's funding.
Nitish Bhardwaj is not the only one to criticise the film for allegedly 'distorting facts'. Mukesh Khanna, Sunil Lahri and others have also raised objections, particularly to Sai Pallavi's portrayal of Sita as a warrior.
Before its release, Ramayana: Part 1 faced criticism over Ranbir Kapoor's casting as Lord Rama and its visual effects. However, audience perception changed after the film hit theatres. It subsequently faced criticism over Sita's portrayal as a warrior wielding a sword and fighting monsters. Despite the criticism, the film has crossed ₹ 860 crore at the domestic box office and ₹ 1,500 crore worldwide. It has also surpassed the lifetime collections of films such as Dhurandhar, Kalki 2898 AD, Jawan, Pathaan and KGF: Chapter 2.
Apart from Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana and Ravi Dubey as Lakshman, the film also stars Rakul Preet Singh, Arun Govil, Lara Dutta and Sheeba Chaddha in key roles. The film has broken several box-office records and continues its strong run in theatres.
